title: Attenuation scenarios and anchor-probes: progressive truncation & retrieval stress plan
content:
Overview:

This doc describes a targeted eval and regression plan for a new model onboarding wave focused on long-context behavior under retrieval pressure and truncation cascades. The goal is to produce deterministic, repeatable probes that exercise: progressive context truncation, retrieval-chaining stress, attention sink insertion, and boundary conditions for KV/attention state retention at 8k / 32k / 128k service lengths.

Why this differs from prior runs:
- Rather than broad recall sweeps, these probes are scenario-driven: they simulate realistic application anchor points (e.g., long legal threads, engineering issue histories, multi-document code notebooks) and then apply deliberate perturbations to retrieval timing and prefix composition to surface degradation onset.
- Emphasis on "attenuation" — how signal strength from earlier context decays as retrievals and truncations stack, not just absolute recall numbers.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Models under test: onboarding candidates for the hosted catalog (open and finetuned variants), 3 variants per model: baseline FP16, 4-bit quant, and fused-kernel optimized build.
- Sequence lengths: 8k, 32k, 128k (we exercise both model max-seq and runtime chunking where applicable).
- Primary acceptance metrics: stable-output-rate (SOR) >= 95% relative to baseline on 8k (for core prompt suite), recall@1 degradation <= 10% when moving from 8k->32k with identical retrieval set, and no >3x increase in p99 latency under canonical batching.
- Secondary metrics: perplexity delta on anchor contexts, token-level edit distance on targeted hallucination probes, cost-per-1k-tokens delta.

Test matrix (high level):
- Axes: sequence length (8k/32k/128k), retrieval payload size (0k/64k/256k), insertion pattern (single anchor, periodic anchor every N tokens, cascading retrievals), truncation policy (truncate-oldest, truncate-near-reply), kernel flags (continuous-batch, kvcache-compact).
- For each cell run N=50 seeded prompts to capture variance (random seeds recorded).

Key probe families and examples:
1) Anchor fidelity probes
- Scenario: a long contract with key clauses at the start; retrieval returns clause snippets interleaved later in the prompt.
- Probe: ask model to extract clause-by-clause summary referencing original clause numbers.
- Failure signal: missing or shuffled clause numbers, confidence mismatches in text references.

2) Thread continuity probes (chat-like)
- Scenario: 150-message engineering thread with code blocks and diffs.
- Probe: given the last 10 messages plus retrievals for older messages, ask for the canonical root cause and top 3 proposed fixes.
- Failure signal: omission of key early context facts, or hallucinated file names.

3) Retrieval-chaining stress
- Scenario: multi-step retrieval where each retrieval depends on previous answers (retrieval->generation->retrieval loop).
- Probe: force 4 chained retrievals with increasing overlap and measure decay in exact-match to ground-truth snippet.
- Failure signal: divergence > 20% exact-match by step 3 for 32k/128k runs.

4) Attention sink insertion tests
- Scenario: insert high-attention garbage (repeated rare tokens + long numeric sequences) in middle-of-context to simulate adversarial sink.
- Probe: evaluate whether anchor references earlier than the sink are still accessible and whether attention distribution shifts (proxy via token importance delta).
- Failure signal: targeted recall drop > 15% for anchors preceding the sink.

5) Progressive truncation cascade
- Scenario: simulate traffic spikes leading to incremental truncation of oldest context.
- Probe: run the same conversation while successively dropping 2k tokens from the head and measure when key answers flip or hallucinations appear.
- Failure signal: key-flip threshold lower than model-specific expectation (documented per-model).

Prompt sets: (naming, not full text for brevity)- legal-anchor-extract-150k: anchored clause extraction with distractors- chat-thread-issue-150: engineering thread recall + code diffs- notebook-provenance-5docs: multi-file code notebook history with provenance questions- customer-email-chain-200: long support chain with action items and dates
Each prompt set includes: canonical ground truth, ranked retrieval pool, and expected answer templates. Prompts are stored in the harness repo linked below.

Measurement & instrumentation:
- Metrics to log per-run: seed id, model_variant, seq_len_requested, seq_len_effective (post-chunking), retrieved_token_count, tokens_read_from_kv, p50/p90/p99 latency, SOR, recall@1/5/10, EM (exact match) for targeted spans, hallucination_flag (binary), prompt_hash, run_duration_ms.
- Tracing: attach opentracing spans through the serving runtime for key phases (parse, retrieve, route, execute, generate).
- KV cache dumps: optional per-failure (configurable) to root cause attention sink behavior — redacted to remove PII.

Regression thresholds and alerting:
- Regression run compares new model vs onboarding baseline. If any of the following triggers, create a regression issue automatically:
  * SOR drop > 5 percentage points on majority of prompt sets at 32k
  * recall@1 drop > 10% aggregated over retrieval-chaining family
  * p99 latency increase > 2x with unchanged batching config
  * hallucination_flag rate increases by absolute 3%
- Alerts post a daily summary to #applied-ml-evals and open JIRA-ML-REGRESSION with attached sample failures and logs.

Test harness & running locally:
- Harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/long-context-harness (see /probes/attenuation)
- Example run command (pseudo):
  ./run_probe --model x.y.onboard.fp16 --promptset notebook-provenance-5docs --seq 32768 --retrieval 256k --runs 50 --output ./results/model_x.y.fp16.32k.json
- CI: onboard PRs must include a smoke run on 8k for the core suite; full 32k/128k runs are nightly and on-demand.

Observed failure modes (hypotheses + early mitigation):
- Rapid attention collapse near long numeric sequences: may indicate softmax scaling mismatch; mitigation: test alternate kernel tiling and norm stabilization before rolling out.
- KV cache fragmentation under chunked execution: probe shows overlapping kv ranges dropped; mitigation: apply conservative kv-compact heuristic and increase chunk overlap for suspect models.
- Retrieval timing race: retrieval arriving late replaces prefixes unexpectedly; mitigation: pin retrieval window and make retrieval insertion atomic in runtime.

Remediation playbook (for SRE/serving/runtime owners):
1) Reproduce locally with exact seed and kernel flags; capture full trace and kv dump.
2) If attention sink suspected, toggle attention scaling / disable fused-kernel path to confirm.
3) If truncation policy causes flip, verify route's truncate policy; consider soft-truncate (metadata-preserving) mode for onboarding.
4) If recall regression persists only on quantized build, flag for quantization fallback (serve FP16 for affected routes).

Appendix A — sample seed prompt (abbreviated):
[BEGIN PROMPT - notebook-provenance-5docs - seed 2983]
Context: Document A (history of edits), Document B (function docstring), Document C (bug report), Document D (test output), Document E (release notes) -- total context 42,312 tokens after retrieval.
Question: "Which code change introduced the regression described in Document C? Provide file, function name, and one-sentence justification referencing the exact line in Document B or A."
Expected: explicit file path + function + line quote (EM match).
[END PROMPT]

Appendix B — quick checklist for onboarding reviewer:
- Run smoke 8k core suite and confirm SOR >= 98%
- Inspect 5 random failures at 32k for hallucination/non-determinism
- Review p99 latency and ensure no >2x regression vs reference
- If any attention-sink failures, gather kv dump and mark for deeper kernel testing

Open questions / next steps:
- How aggressive should automatic fallback be for quant builds vs latency targets? (ops + product tradeoff)
- Decide canonical truncation policy: preserve latest N tokens vs preserve N tokens around last system message.
- Add synthetic adversarial sink corpus to add coverage to nightly runs.

Notes to self / TODOs:

- Coordinate with runtime to add kv dump toggle flag accessible from CI.
- Schedule demo with product and SRE for March onboarding wave.
